citations.title: Assessment and service plan requirements
citations.requirement: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition must be completed by a physician, physician assistant or APRN. It must be repeated at least annually and on a significant change in condition, including a diagnosis of Alzheimer's or a related dementia. IDPH may set more frequent skin-integrity and nutrition assessments by rule. A written service plan is mutually agreed by provider, resident and representative and reviewed at least annually or when needs change. On request the resident or representative gets a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan. Text as amended by P.A. 104-0589.

citations.title: Issuance of license
citations.requirement: A full-time director must be 21+ with a high school diploma or equivalent plus qualifying experience (35(a)(2)). Staff must be sufficient in number and skill for 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs and must take ongoing training (35(a)(3)). All employees subject to the Health Care Worker Background Check Act must meet it (35(a)(4)). Applicant must file the Alzheimer's/dementia special care disclosure document (35(a)(7)). As a condition of licensure the director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years. Licenses last one year, state the physical location, issue and expiration dates, and are not transferable.

citations.title: Service requirements
citations.requirement: Defines medication reminders, supervision of self-administered medication and medication administration. Medication administration is by a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment. A certified medication aide may administer under RN supervision and delegation per Nurse Practice Act 50-75, except Schedule II controlled substances and any subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal or IV medication. Supervision of self-administered medication is under a licensed health care professional, or under RN delegation for a certified medication aide. IDPH sets procedures by rule. Services may be provided directly or by others arranged with resident consent.

citations.title: Civil penalties
citations.requirement: IDPH may assess a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation, with each day a separate violation. A penalty of up to $3,000 (also per day) may be assessed for caring for a resident who exceeds the care needs defined in the Act. Repeated technical infractions within a calendar year may become a Type 3 violation. IDPH may hold hearings on appeals.

citations.title: Alzheimer and dementia programs
citations.requirement: No admission or retention if the establishment cannot provide or secure appropriate care or lacks appropriately skilled staff. Residency is barred if the resident's condition has so deteriorated that residency is detrimental to the resident or others, or if the resident is dangerous and the danger cannot be eliminated. IDPH rule must identify a validated dementia-specific assessment standard with inter-rater reliability. That assessment is approved by the physician, or a PA/APRN with geriatric dementia experience. It is done before acceptance, annually, and on a change in condition. Annual and change-of-condition assessments must be signed by a physician. Establishments offering a special dementia program must disclose to IDPH and residents, ensure a designated representative, adopt wandering and evacuation safety policies, coordinate communications with family, provide cognitive stimulation and activities, staff appropriately, provide director and direct care staff dementia training, and have emergency procedures and staffing patterns. Pre-admission assessment tools must be validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment (150(g)).

citations.title: Amends 210 ILCS 9/15, 35, 70, 135 and 150
citations.requirement: Amends Sections 15, 35, 70, 135 and 150 of the Assisted Living and Shared Housing Act. Section 99 makes it effective on becoming law. The ILGA page shows Effective Date 7/24/2026.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: Requires sufficient qualified staff for 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs (a). Requires at least one direct care staff person on duty at all times with adult CPR training (including a skills demonstration) and current certification (b). Direct care staff must be 16+ at hire (c). Job descriptions must set minimum education and experience (d). Employee files must hold the items in (e) and (f). Records are kept for employment plus at least 12 months (g). Staffing must cover the services listed in (h). Personnel schedules must meet (i). Awake staff are required for residents who cannot self-move to safety (j). Shared housing needs at least one staff member on site at all times (k). Assisted living needs at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours (l). Nurse Aide Registry check before hire, with no hiring of anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation (m). Licensed-staff license verification (n). Cornell shows this section's history as last amended in 2004, so check it against the current JCAR text.

citations.title: Establishment Contracts
citations.requirement: The contract must be titled 'assisted living establishment contract' or 'shared housing establishment contract' and printed in at least 12-point type. It must contain the 20 elements in (a), including: license status; base rate and services; extra services and fee schedule; complaint process with notice of the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; the Medicaid statement; admission and termination criteria; a risk management statement; and the Section 95 rights list. It must also include a statement from IDPH on the annual on-site review process. Under (b) it must include fee/deposit/refund terms, 30 days' written notice of fee changes (not required where service needs change per the service plan), and an emergency/relative notification policy. A copy goes to the resident or representative, and the signed contract stays on premises. Contracts may auto-renew yearly, and changes must be written and signed by both parties.

citations.title: License requirement
citations.requirement: No person may establish, operate, maintain or offer an assisted living or shared housing establishment without a license (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Renewal of licenses
citations.requirement: Renewal application is filed 120-150 days before expiration. IDPH 'may' grant a 2-year renewal at the licensee's request only if, in the preceding 24 months, there was no Type 1 or Type 2 violation, no inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and no admission or retention in violation of Section 75 (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Application for License
citations.requirement: Nonrefundable fee of $2,000 + $20 per unit for assisted living, $1,000 for shared housing. The application states standard vs. floating licensure, includes liability insurance documentation, and shows financial capacity (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Initial license issuance
citations.requirement: IDPH issues a regular license within 120 days of a complete application. Approval needs fees paid, substantial compliance, and Background Check Act compliance for covered employees (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Residency Requirements
citations.requirement: An establishment may not accept or retain a resident when it lacks staff appropriate in numbers and skill, or cannot provide or secure the required services (per fact-checked research). Read the full text for the complete list of conditions.

citations.title: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
citations.requirement: Covers employees with or who may have resident contact. Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Supportive Living Program
citations.requirement: HFS rules for Medicaid Supportive Living. Applies only if the facility is separately approved and certified by HFS. It does not apply to an IDPH-licensed establishment that is private pay only.

citations.title: Assisted Living and Shared Housing Establishment Code
citations.requirement: Subparts, as confirmed on the LII table of contents: A General Provisions (295.1-295.1110); B Policies (295.2000-295.2080); C Personnel (295.3000-295.3050); D Resident Care and Services (295.4000-295.4060); E Medications (295.5000); F Resident Rights (295.6000-295.6030); G Resident and Establishment Records (295.7000-295.7010); H Food Service (295.8000); I Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (295.9000-295.9040). The LII notes show amendments through 7/29/2024.

policies.category: Subpart A – General Provisions: § 295.500 Application for License
policies.title: IDPH License Application, Standard vs. Floating Licensure, Renewal and Posting
state_specifics: No person may establish, operate, maintain or offer an establishment without an IDPH license (210 ILCS 9/25)
The application must state whether standard or floating licensure is requested. A floating-license application must comply with Section 32 of the Act and Section 295.1110
The nonrefundable fee is $2,000 + $20 per licensed unit (assisted living) or $1,000 (shared housing), paid with the application
IDPH issues a regular license within 120 days of a complete application. Licenses last one year, state the physical location and are not transferable

The renewal application is due 120-150 days before expiration. A 2-year renewal is available only with no Type 1 or Type 2 violation in 24 months, no inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and no Section 75 admission or retention violation

policies.category: Subpart A – General Provisions: § 295.500 Application for License
policies.title: Service Delivery Contract Verification and Standard Contract Copy for IDPH
state_specifics: Each resident or resident's representative must sign an establishment contract that meets Section 295.2030
The application must verify that the establishment has entered or will enter into such a contract with each resident
A copy of the standard contract offered to residents is filed with the application
The signed contract is kept on the premises, and the administrator re-files the standard contract when IDPH rules change

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2000 Residency Requirements
policies.title: Admission Eligibility: Who May and May Not Be Accepted (Functional and Behavioral Criteria)
state_specifics: Do not accept or retain anyone whose needs the establishment cannot provide or secure, whose needs are outside its license, or when staff lack the numbers or skill. Only adults are accepted
Do not accept anyone who poses a serious threat to self or others
Do not accept anyone who cannot communicate needs in any manner, unless a resident representative who lives in the establishment and had a prior relationship has been appointed to direct services
Do not accept anyone who needs total assistance with 2 or more ADLs, or more than one paid caregiver at a time for an ADL
Do not accept anyone who needs more than minimal assistance to reach a safe area in an emergency, meaning they cannot respond with or without assistance given staffing and construction

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2000 Residency Requirements
policies.title: Admission Exclusions: Severe Mental Illness and Clinical Treatment Conditions
state_specifics: Severe mental illness is a DSM-5-TR major mental disorder with substantial disability expected to last at least one year. Alzheimer's and other organic dementias are excluded from this definition, and a diagnosis of depression alone does not bar residency

IV therapy or feedings, gastrostomy feedings, catheter insertion or sterile irrigation or replacement (routine urinary catheter maintenance is allowed), sterile wound care, and routine insulin injections are barred unless self-administered or given by a licensed health care professional
The licensed professional for these services may not be employed by the owner or operator, its parent, or any commonly owned entity or affiliate. The resident keeps the right to choose a provider
Do not accept anyone needing treatment of stage 3 or 4 decubitus ulcers or exfoliative dermatitis
Do not accept anyone needing 5 or more skilled nursing visits per week for 3 or more consecutive weeks, except a rehabilitative course certified temporary by a physician

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2000 Residency Requirements
policies.title: Residency Exceptions (Hospice, Physical Disability) and Pre-Admission Vaccine Advice
state_specifics: Terminally ill residents may remain if they receive or qualify for hospice coordinated by a licensed hospice program or a licensed professional employed by a licensed home health agency, and the establishment and all parties agree

The (c)(3), (4), (5) and (9) exclusions do not apply to quadriplegic, paraplegic or neuro-muscular disease residents who can communicate, need no complex medical assistance, and whose needs the establishment can meet

An establishment that does not offer medication administration must advise each prospective resident before admission to consult a physician about pneumococcal pneumonia and/or influenza vaccination (Act Sec. 76)
Document the vaccine advice in the admission file

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2010 Termination of Residency
policies.title: Termination of Residency, Discharge and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Residency must be terminated under Section 295.2010 if the resident develops a condition listed in 295.2000(c), unless the hospice exception applies
Residency must be terminated under Section 295.2010 when available services no longer meet the resident's needs. IDPH may also require termination
Notice periods and grounds must be copied from the 295.2010 rule text before adoption (text not retrieved)
Caring for a resident who exceeds the Act's care needs can draw a civil penalty of up to $3,000 per day (210 ILCS 9/135)
Admission and termination criteria must also appear in the resident contract (295.2030(a))

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2020 Notice of Closure
policies.title: Facility Closure Notice and Resident Relocation
state_specifics: Closure notice deadlines to IDPH and residents must be taken from the 295.2020 rule text (not retrieved)
Designate the administrator to lead relocation planning and notify representatives, the Ombudsman and IDPH
Keep resident records available after closure per the Records policy
Resident funds and deposits must be accounted for and refunded under the contract refund policy

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2030 Establishment Contracts
policies.title: Assisted Living / Shared Housing Establishment Contract: Required Form and Content
state_specifics: The title must read "assisted living establishment contract" or "shared housing establishment contract", printed in at least 12-point type

The 20 required elements include the establishment name and street and mailing address, and the name and address of at least one natural person authorized to accept service for owners and the managing agent
The contract must describe the establishment's license status and that of every provider of health-related or supportive services arranged by the establishment
It must state the contract duration. Contracts may auto-renew yearly, and changes must be written and signed by both parties

It must include the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and Long-Term Care Ombudsman notice, a statement that Medicaid (Public Aid Code Articles V/VI) is not available, a risk management statement, the Section 95 rights list, and the IDPH annual on-site review statement

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2030 Establishment Contracts
policies.title: Fees, Deposits, Refunds, Fee-Change Notice and Emergency Notification
state_specifics: The contract states terms of occupancy, including resident responsibilities and obligations
It states the amount and purpose of every fee, charge and deposit, including any charge for days a resident is absent
It states the refund policy for fees, charges and deposits
Give at least 30 days' written notice before any fee or charge change. This is not required for an increase resulting from changed service needs documented in the service plan

It states the policy for notifying a relative or other designated person of an emergency, a significant change in condition, or termination of residency. A copy of the signed contract goes to the resident or representative

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2030 Establishment Contracts
policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Any resident funds handled by staff require a written authorization and a separate itemized ledger
Deposit and refund handling must follow the contract's stated refund policy
Contract fee schedules must be consistent with what is billed
Do not commingle resident funds with operating funds

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2040 Disaster Preparedness
policies.title: Written Disaster Plan: Relocation, Severe Weather and Power Outages
state_specifics: The plan must protect all persons by keeping them in place, moving them to areas of refuge, and evacuating the building when necessary
It must address residents' physical and cognitive needs and special staff response, and be revised whenever a resident with unusual needs is admitted
It must provide for temporary relocation of residents in any disaster requiring relocation
It must provide for moving residents to safe locations within the building for a National Weather Service tornado warning or severe thunderstorm warning
It must address power outages. Dementia programs must also have emergency procedures and staffing patterns (210 ILCS 9/150)

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2040 Disaster Preparedness
policies.title: Heat, Cold and Temperature Extremes
state_specifics: Temporarily relocate residents whenever bedroom temperatures fall below 55°F for 12 hours or more due to a mechanical problem or power loss
When the heat index/apparent temperature (Section 295 Table A) exceeds 80°F in living, dining, activity or sleeping areas, provide for residents' health, safety, welfare and comfort
Monitor and log indoor temperatures and the heat index daily during hot weather
Table A (heat index) is part of the Subpart I appendices

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2040 Disaster Preparedness
policies.title: Emergency Drills and Written Drill Evaluations
state_specifics: A written evaluation of each drill goes to the establishment manager
Keep each drill evaluation for one year from the date of the drill
Drill frequencies and evaluation content must be taken from the 295.2040 text (not retrieved in full)
Use the same drill records for survey review

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2050 Incident and Accident Reporting
policies.title: Serious Incident and Accident Reporting to IDPH
state_specifics: Report any serious incident or accident to IDPH. "Serious" means any incident or accident that causes physical or emotional harm or injury to a resident
A change in condition due to health or medical decline is not a reportable incident or accident
Report within 24 hours to the IDPH Division of Assisted Living by email at DPH.LTCAL@illinois.gov, or as the Department requests
Keep a copy of the report for one year after the incident or accident
Notify the resident's representative or designated relative per the contract notification policy

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2060 Quality Improvement Program
policies.title: Quality Improvement Program
state_specifics: The program covers oversight and monitoring, resident satisfaction, and ongoing quality improvement with implementation of any improvement plan
The process must benchmark performance, be customer-centered, data-driven and focused on resident satisfaction
A system must detect issues and problems, expedite action and resolve problems
Proof of an ongoing program is part of the license application (295.500(a)(8))
Minute QI meetings, track incidents, grievances and satisfaction surveys, and keep the records survey-ready

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2070 Negotiated Risk Agreement
policies.title: Negotiated Risk Agreements
state_specifics: Required content must be taken from the 295.2070 text (not retrieved)
Use only with the resident or representative's informed agreement
Document the risk, the resident's choice and the mitigation plan
Reference the agreement in the service plan and the risk management statement in the contract

policies.category: Subpart B – Policies: § 295.2080 Essential Support Persons
policies.title: Essential Support Persons and Resident Access
state_specifics: The rule governs essential support persons (visitation and access). Detailed terms must be taken from the 295.2080 text (not retrieved)
Residents may designate an essential support person
Record the designation in the resident file
Visiting restrictions must not override resident rights

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Staffing Sufficiency, Supervision and Personnel Schedules
state_specifics: Staff must be sufficient in number, qualifications, skills, education and experience to meet 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs, and must take part in ongoing training
Staffing must cover mandatory services, service plan services, general supervision and crisis intervention, food service, environmental services, evacuation and optional services
The personnel schedule shows date, scheduled hours, and name and position of each employee, reflects actual hours worked, and is kept 12 months after the last date on the schedule
If residents cannot independently move to safety, enough staff must be present and awake to move them to a safe area 24 hours a day
Review staffing against resident acuity at each assessment

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: 24-Hour On-Site Coverage and CPR-Certified Direct Care Staff
state_specifics: Assisted living: at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours a day

Shared housing: at least one staff member on site at all times. The only exception is a brief absence (emergency room or grocery trip), with arrangements to monitor resident safety per the service delivery plan
At least one direct care staff person with current adult CPR certification, including a demonstrated skills check, is on duty at all times
Track CPR expirations and schedule so every shift has a certified person

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Job Descriptions, Minimum Age, Employee Files and Personnel Record Retention
state_specifics: Direct care staff must be 16 or older on the start date
Job descriptions state minimum education and experience
Every file holds name, date of birth, home address, SSN and phone; documentation of freedom from pulmonary TB, orientation and ongoing training; and start and end dates
Direct care files also hold CPR certification if applicable, initial health evaluation, Background Check Act compliance, and the Nurse Aide Registry check
Keep records throughout employment and at least 12 months after the last date of employment, unless law requires longer

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Nurse Aide Registry, Health Care Worker Background Checks and License Verification
state_specifics: Check all applicants on the Nurse Aide Registry before hiring. Do not hire anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property
Before hiring into a position requiring a State professional license, contact the Illinois Department of Professional Regulation to verify an active license, and file a copy of the verification
Employees with resident contact must meet the Health Care Worker Background Check Act
Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to Illinois State Police within 10 working days
Licensure approval requires covered employees to meet the Act (295.600)

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Manager / Director Qualifications, Training and Manager Changes
state_specifics: A full-time director/manager must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent plus qualifying experience (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(2))
As a condition of licensure the director must complete at least 20 hours of training every 2 years (210 ILCS 9/35)
A shared housing manager may oversee up to three establishments within 30 minutes' drive who are immediately reachable. Pinpoint this in 295.3010 before adoption
Report a manager change to IDPH within 10 working days. Pinpoint this in 295.3010
P.A. 104-0589 amended Section 35, so check the current director-qualification text

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Employee Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Staff must take part in ongoing training to serve the resident population (295.3000(a))
Orientation and in-service topics and hours must be taken from the 295.3020 text (not retrieved)
Document orientation and ongoing training in each employee file
The director and direct care staff in dementia programs must receive dementia training (210 ILCS 9/150)
Include bloodborne pathogen training (OSHA) for staff with exposure risk

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Employee Health Evaluation and TB Screening
state_specifics: Direct care and food service employees need an initial health evaluation (295.3030). Timing and content come from the rule text (not retrieved)
Every employee file must document freedom from pulmonary TB (295.3000(e))
TB skin test steps and timing come from the 295.4050 text (not retrieved)
Exclude ill employees per the communicable disease policy

policies.category: Subpart C – Personnel: § 295.3000 Personnel Requirements, Qualifications and Training
policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Prohibit abuse, neglect, exploitation and misappropriation of resident property. Violations are reported per the abuse reporting policy
Staff may not accept gifts, loans or financial transactions from residents
Anyone with a Nurse Aide Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation cannot be employed
Staff sign a code of conduct at hire

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Pre-Admission Comprehensive Assessment, Reassessment and Service Plan
state_specifics: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition must be completed by a physician, PA or APRN (210 ILCS 9/15 as amended by P.A. 104-0589, effective 7/24/2026)
Repeat at least annually and on a significant change in condition, including a diagnosis of Alzheimer's or related dementia
IDPH may require more frequent skin-integrity and nutrition assessments by rule
The service plan is mutually agreed by the provider, resident and representative, and reviewed at least annually or when needs change

On request, give the resident or representative a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan. Reconcile the 'physician' wording of 295.4000 with the Act

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Mandatory and Optional Services Offered
state_specifics: List all mandatory services from 295.4020 (rule text not retrieved)
List each optional service the establishment offers, such as medication administration, with its fee
The list goes to IDPH with the license application and into the contract
Services may be provided directly or arranged with the resident's consent (210 ILCS 9/70)

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Communicable Disease, TB and Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Written communicable disease policies are required (295.4040). Content comes from the rule text (not retrieved)
TB skin test procedures follow 295.4050 (not retrieved)
Offer pneumococcal and influenza vaccine advice per 295.2000(i) if medication administration is not offered
Follow the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard for exposure control
Report communicable disease outbreaks as required by public health rules

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia Care Programs
state_specifics: An applicant must file the Alzheimer's/dementia special care disclosure document (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7))

Assessments must use an IDPH-identified validated dementia-specific tool, approved by the physician or a PA/APRN with geriatric dementia experience, before acceptance, annually and on change in condition
Annual and change-of-condition dementia assessments must be signed by a physician

A special dementia program must disclose to IDPH and residents, ensure a designated representative, adopt wandering and evacuation safety policies, coordinate family communication, provide cognitive stimulation and activities, staff appropriately and train staff
Rule-level staffing and training numbers come from 295.4060 (not retrieved)

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: A significant change in condition triggers a reassessment and service plan review (210 ILCS 9/15)
A health or medical decline alone is not a reportable incident (295.2050(a)), but any resulting serious harm is
Notify the representative or designated person per the contract policy
Re-evaluate against the 295.2000(c) exclusion criteria after any change
Document each notification in the resident record

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: IDPH may set more frequent skin-integrity and nutrition assessments by rule (210 ILCS 9/15)
Do not retain residents needing treatment of stage 3 or 4 decubitus ulcers (295.2000(c)(12))
A fall causing injury is a serious incident reportable within 24 hours
Include fall and skin risk in the service plan

policies.category: Subpart D – Resident Care and Services (§ 295.4000–295.4060)
policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination; Death of a Resident
state_specifics: A terminally ill resident may stay if hospice is coordinated by a licensed hospice or licensed home-health professional and all parties agree (295.2000(f))
Revise the service plan with the hospice plan of care
Follow the contract notification policy on a resident's death
Resident funds, deposits and refunds are settled per the contract refund policy

policies.category: Subpart E – Medications (§ 295.5000)
policies.title: Medication Reminders, Self-Administration Supervision, Administration, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: The Act defines medication reminders, supervision of self-administered medication and medication administration (210 ILCS 9/70)
Medication administration is by a licensed health care professional employed by the establishment
Storage and procedural requirements come from 295.5000 (not retrieved)
Describe the service level offered in the contract and service plan
P.A. 104-0589 amended Section 70, so review the current text

policies.category: Subpart E – Medications (§ 295.5000)
policies.title: Certified Medication Aides and RN Delegation
state_specifics: A certified medication aide may administer medication under RN supervision and delegation per Nurse Practice Act Sec. 50-75
Excluded: Schedule II controlled substances and any subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal or IV medication
Supervision of self-administered medication is under a licensed professional, or under RN delegation for a certified medication aide
Verify each license and certification before assigning duties

policies.category: Subpart F – Resident Rights (§ 295.6000–295.6030)
policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: The contract must list the Section 95 rights and state that signing does not forfeit them
Full rights text comes from 295.6000 and Section 95 (not retrieved)
Post and distribute rights at admission and keep a signed acknowledgment
Train staff on rights at orientation

policies.category: Subpart F – Resident Rights (§ 295.6000–295.6030)
policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Reporting recipients, time frames and training come from 295.6010 (not retrieved)
Do not hire anyone with a Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation
Report serious harm to IDPH within 24 hours at DPH.LTCAL@illinois.gov
Protect residents from retaliation
Civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation per day

policies.category: Subpart F – Resident Rights (§ 295.6000–295.6030)
policies.title: Resident's Representative and Advance Directives
state_specifics: Representative rules come from 295.6030 (not retrieved)
A representative may sign the contract
A resident who cannot communicate needs requires an appointed representative who lives in the establishment with a prior relationship (295.2000(c)(2))
Keep advance directives in the resident record and note them in the service plan

policies.category: Subpart F – Resident Rights (§ 295.6000–295.6030)
policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: The contract must describe the complaint process and give notice of the Department on Aging Senior Helpline and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
Give the Ombudsman access to residents
Log every grievance and its resolution and feed it to the QI program
No retaliation against a complainant

policies.category: Subpart F – Resident Rights (§ 295.6000–295.6030)
policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Restrict access to resident records to authorized staff
Release information only with authorization or as law permits
Apply HIPAA where the establishment is a covered entity, and confirm status
Report breaches per policy

policies.category: Subpart F – Resident Rights (§ 295.6000–295.6030)
policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Provide reasonable accommodations for disabilities
Provide interpreters or translated materials as needed
Admission decisions rest on the 295.2000 criteria, not protected characteristics
Title VI applies if federal funds (for example, SLP Medicaid) are received

policies.category: Subpart G – Resident and Establishment Records (§ 295.7000–295.7010)
policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Retention periods come from 295.7000-7010 (not retrieved)
Keep the signed contract on premises
Keep assessments, service plans and the documents the annual on-site reviewer examines (295.2030(a)(20))
Keep incident reports one year and drill evaluations one year

policies.category: Subpart G – Resident and Establishment Records (§ 295.7000–295.7010)
policies.title: Required Reports to IDPH and Annual On-Site Review
state_specifics: Serious incidents are reported within 24 hours by email to DPH.LTCAL@illinois.gov
The contract includes an IDPH statement on the annual on-site review process
Renewal is filed 120-150 days before expiration
Report manager changes within 10 working days (confirm in 295.3010)

policies.category: Subpart H – Food Service (§ 295.8000)
policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Menu, diet and sanitation requirements come from 295.8000 (not retrieved)
Staffing must cover food service if provided (295.3000(h))
Food service employees need an initial health evaluation (295.3030)
IDPH may require periodic nutrition assessments

policies.category: Subpart I – Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (§ 295.9000–295.9040)
policies.title: Physical Plant, Units, Furnishings and Construction Plan Review
state_specifics: Standards are in 295.9000, 9005 (Units), 9010 (assisted living), 9020 (shared housing) and 9030 (Furnishings)
New construction or major alteration requires IDPH-approved drawings before work begins
IDPH gives a completeness notice within 10 working days and approves or disapproves within 45 calendar days
IDPH Design and Construction performs the pre-licensure survey

policies.category: Subpart I – Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (§ 295.9000–295.9040)
policies.title: Environmental Requirements, Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Environmental standards come from 295.9040 (not retrieved)
Heat index monitoring is tied to Table A
Staffing must cover environmental services (295.3000(h)(5))
Keep a preventive maintenance log

policies.category: Subpart I – Physical Plant and Environmental Requirements (§ 295.9000–295.9040)
policies.title: Fire Safety, Life Safety Code and Evacuation
state_specifics: IDPH Design and Construction conducts the Life Safety Code survey before licensure
Staffing must cover evacuation of residents (295.3000(h)(6))
Sufficient awake staff must be present to move impaired residents to safety
Test and document fire systems and keep tags current. Confirm the system requirements with IDPH and the local fire authority

policies.category: Governance and Administration
policies.title: Governing Body, Administrator Responsibilities and Policy Review
state_specifics: The licensee is responsible for compliance with the Act and Part 295
A full-time director/manager is required
Review policies annually and when rules change, including after P.A. 104-0589
Keep a version log

policies.category: Governance and Administration
policies.title: Regulatory Compliance, Surveys, Civil Penalties and Corporate Compliance
state_specifics: Civil penalty up to $5,000 per violation, each day a separate violation
Up to $3,000 per day for caring for a resident who exceeds the Act's care needs
Repeated technical infractions within a calendar year can become a Type 3 violation
Type 1/2 and Type 3 violation history affects 2-year renewal eligibility
Billing and fee practices must match the contract

policies.category: Governance and Administration
policies.title: Supportive Living Program Participation (if applicable)
state_specifics: Medicaid does not pay in IDPH-licensed assisted living or shared housing; the contract must say so
Applies only if HFS separately approves and certifies the site under 89 Ill. Adm. Code 146
HFS contact: 1-844-528-8444, HFS.SLF@illinois.gov
Omit this policy for private-pay-only operations

policies.category: Safety and Protection
policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Dementia programs must adopt wandering and evacuation safety policies (210 ILCS 9/150)
Missing resident events with harm are serious incidents reportable within 24 hours
Staff must be awake and able to supervise at all times
Run a missing resident drill

policies.category: Safety and Protection
policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Resident rights (Section 95 and 295.6000) govern freedom from restraint; confirm the exact rule text
Do not restrain for staff convenience
Use of restraint harming a resident may be abuse
Document any resident-specific safety measure in a negotiated risk agreement or service plan

policies.category: Daily Living
policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Dementia programs must provide cognitive stimulation and activities (210 ILCS 9/150)
Offer activities suited to resident interests and abilities
Record optional activities and fees in the contract
Review participation in the QI program

policies.category: Daily Living
policies.title: Transportation, Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Transportation arrangements and fees must be stated in the contract
Smoking rules must be written and shared at admission
Visiting is subject to resident rights and the essential support person rule
Pet rules are set by the establishment and must be disclosed in the contract
Shared housing staff absences for transport need safety coverage (295.3000(k))

documents.how_used: <cite index="1-1">IDPH's Assisted Living page lists only a complaint form, involuntary-termination forms and a Life Safety Code inspection request.</cite> I found no policy-review checklist or application packet on it. Items below come from the Part 295 sections that list required written policies and plans. I fetched § 295.500, § 295.2000 and § 295.3000 in full. § 295.2030, § 295.2040, § 295.2050 and § 295.2060 came from search excerpts, so they are partial or condensed. Cornell LII mirrors: https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/title-77/part-295/subpart-B and https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/Ill-Admin-Code-tit-77-SS-295.3000

required_items.text: Verification that the establishment has entered or will enter into a service delivery contract as provided in Section 295.2030 with each resident or resident's representative.
Proof of an ongoing quality improvement program in accordance with Section 295.2060.
Information about the mandatory and optional services to be provided at the establishment.
A copy of the standard contract offered to residents.
The application shall indicate a request for either standard licensure or floating licensure. A floating-license application shall comply with Section 32 of the Act and Section 295.1110.

No individual shall be accepted for residency or remain in residence if the establishment cannot provide or secure appropriate services. The same applies if the individual needs a level or type of service the establishment is not licensed for or does not provide, or if it lacks staff appropriate in numbers and skill.
Only adults may be accepted for residency.
Not accepted if the person poses a serious threat to themselves or others.

Not accepted if the person cannot communicate their needs in any manner and no resident representative residing in the establishment, with a prior relationship to the person, has been appointed to direct services.
Not accepted if the person requires total assistance with 2 or more activities of daily living.
Not accepted if the person requires the assistance of more than one paid caregiver at any given time with an activity of daily living.

Not accepted if the person requires more than minimal assistance in moving to a safe area in an emergency. Minimal assistance means the resident can respond, with or without assistance, to protect themselves given the staffing and construction of the building.

Not accepted if the person has a severe mental illness as defined in the Section (DSM-5-TR major mental disorder with substantial disability expected to last at least one year). Alzheimer's disease and other dementias based on organic or physical disorders are excluded from this definition. A diagnosis of depression alone does not bar residency unless the resident is substantially disabled in the listed areas.
Not accepted if the person requires intravenous therapy or feedings, unless self-administered or administered by a qualified, licensed health care professional.
Not accepted if the person requires gastrostomy feedings, unless self-administered or administered by a licensed health care professional.

Not accepted if the person requires insertion, sterile irrigation and replacement of a catheter, except routine maintenance of urinary catheters, unless care is self-administered or administered by a licensed health care professional.
Not accepted if the person requires sterile wound care, unless self-administered or administered by a licensed health care professional.
Not accepted if the person is a diabetic requiring routine insulin injections, unless self-administered or administered by a licensed health care professional.
Not accepted if the person requires treatment of stage 3 or stage 4 decubitus ulcers or exfoliative dermatitis.

Not accepted if the person requires 5 or more skilled nursing visits per week for conditions other than those in (c)(12), for 3 consecutive weeks or more. The exception is a course of treatment expected to extend beyond 3 weeks for rehabilitative purposes and certified as temporary by a physician.
A resident with a condition listed in subsection (c) shall have residency terminated in accordance with Section 295.2010.

Residency shall be terminated in accordance with Section 295.2010 when services available in the establishment are no longer adequate to meet the resident's needs. This does not limit the Department's authority to require termination of residency.

Subsection (d) does not apply to terminally ill residents who receive or would qualify for hospice care coordinated by a licensed hospice program or by a licensed health care professional employed by a licensed home health agency, when the establishment and all parties agree to continued residency.

Subsections (c)(3), (4), (5) and (9) do not apply to quadriplegic or paraplegic individuals, or those with neuro-muscular diseases or other chronic conditions. This holds if the individual can communicate their needs, does not need assistance with complex medical problems, and the establishment can accommodate their needs.

For (c)(7)–(10), the licensed health care professional may not be employed by the owner or operator, its parent entity, or any entity with common ownership, including affiliates. Nothing limits a resident's right to choose their health care provider.

Before admission to an establishment that does not provide medication administration as an optional service, the establishment shall advise the prospective resident to consult a physician about pneumococcal pneumonia and/or influenza vaccination.

The contract must be entitled "assisted living establishment contract" or "shared housing establishment contract" as applicable. It must be printed in no less than 12 point type and include at least the listed elements (a)(1)–(6) in the body or in supporting documents or attachments. The excerpt I retrieved showed (a)(1), (a)(4), (a)(5) and (a)(6).
The name, street address and mailing address of the establishment.
The name and address of at least one natural person authorized to accept service on behalf of the owners and managing agent.
A statement describing the establishment's license status and the license status of all providers of health-related or supportive services to a resident under arrangement with the establishment.
The duration of the contract.
<cite index="46-4">Terms of occupancy, including resident responsibilities and obligations.</cite>
<cite index="46-4">The amount and purpose of any fee, charge and deposit, including any fee or charge for days a resident is absent.</cite>
<cite index="46-4">The establishment's policy for refunding fees, charges or deposits.</cite>

<cite index="46-4,46-5">The establishment's responsibility to give at least 30 days written notice before any change in a fee or charge. A licensee need not give 30 days notice of an increase for a resident whose service needs change, as documented in the service plan.</cite>

<cite index="46-5">The establishment's policy concerning notification of a relative or other individual in an emergency, significant change in the resident's condition, or termination of residency.</cite>

<cite index="16-5">Have a written plan for protection of all persons in the event of disasters, for keeping persons in place, for evacuating persons to areas of refuge, and for evacuating persons from the building when necessary.</cite> <cite index="16-6,16-7">The plan shall address the physical and cognitive needs of residents and include special staff response, including procedures needed to ensure the safety of any resident. It shall be amended or revised whenever a resident with unusual needs is admitted.</cite>
<cite index="18-6">Provide for the temporary relocation of residents for any disaster requiring relocation.</cite>

<cite index="18-6">Provide for the movement of residents to safe locations within the establishment in the event of a tornado warning or severe thunderstorm warning issued by the National Weather Service.</cite>

<cite index="16-8">Provide for the temporary relocation of residents any time the temperature in residents' bedrooms falls below 55°F for 12 hours or more because of a mechanical problem or loss of power.</cite>

<cite index="16-8">Provide for the health, safety, welfare and comfort of all residents when the heat index/apparent temperature (Section 295.Table A) inside living, dining, activities or sleeping areas exceeds 80°F.</cite>
<cite index="16-8">Address power outages.</cite>

<cite index="16-8">A written evaluation of each drill shall be submitted to the establishment manager and maintained for one year from the date of the drill.</cite> The evaluation content list was cut off in the excerpt I retrieved.

<cite index="27-2,27-3">An establishment shall report to the Department any serious incident or accident. "Serious" means any incident or accident that causes physical or emotional harm or injury to a resident.</cite> <cite index="27-4">A change in a resident's condition due to health or medical decline is not a reportable incident or accident.</cite>

<cite index="27-5">The report shall be made to the IDPH Division of Assisted Living by email at DPH.LTCAL@illinois.gov, or as the Department requests, within 24 hours after the incident or accident.</cite>
<cite index="27-6">A copy of the report shall be maintained by the establishment for one year after the date of the incident or accident.</cite>

<cite index="60-3,60-4">The establishment shall establish an effective quality improvement program covering oversight and monitoring, resident satisfaction, and ongoing quality improvement and implementation of any plan for improved quality services. The process must benchmark performance, be customer centered, be data driven, and focus on resident satisfaction.</cite>
<cite index="60-6">A system shall be in place to facilitate the detection of issues and problems, to expedite the implementation of action, and to resolve problems.</cite>

The establishment shall have staff sufficient in number, with qualifications, adequate skills, education and experience, to meet the 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs of residents. Staff shall take part in ongoing training to serve the resident population.
At least one direct care staff person with current adult CPR certification, including a demonstration of ability, shall be on duty at all times.
At the starting date of employment, each direct care staff member shall be 16 years of age or older.
Job descriptions shall define the minimum education and experience requirements for staff.

A file shall be maintained for each employee containing: (1) name, date of birth, home address, Social Security number and telephone number; (2) documentation of (A) freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis, (B) employee orientation and (C) ongoing training; and (3) starting and ending dates of employment.

The file for each direct care employee shall also contain documentation of: (1) current CPR certification, if applicable; (2) initial health evaluation; (3) compliance with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act; and (4) that the employer checked the employee's status with the Nurse Aide Registry.

Records required by this Section shall be maintained throughout employment or service and for at least 12 months after the last date of employment or service, unless State or federal law requires longer.

Sufficient personnel to provide for the current resident population: (1) all mandatory services; (2) services in each resident's service plan; (3) service to meet each resident's needs, including 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs, general supervision and the ability to intervene in a crisis; (4) food services, if provided; (5) environmental services; (6) evacuation of residents during emergencies; and (7) any optional services stated in the service plan.

The personnel schedule shall: (1) indicate date, scheduled work hours, and name and position of each employee assigned; (2) reflect actual work hours; and (3) be maintained and available on request for at least 12 months after the last date on the schedule.

If the establishment accepts individuals with impairments that prevent them from independently moving to an area of safety, sufficient staff must be present and awake to enable these residents to move to a safe area 24 hours per day.

Shared housing establishments shall have at least one staff member on site at all times. The only exceptions are brief absences, such as an emergency room trip or grocery trip. In those cases, arrangements shall be made to monitor resident safety in accordance with the service delivery plan.
Assisted living establishments shall have at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours per day.

The establishment shall check all applicants with the Nurse Aide Registry before hiring. It is prohibited from hiring anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property on the Registry.

Before employing anyone in a position that requires a State professional license, the establishment shall contact the Illinois Department of Professional Regulation to verify the license is active. A copy of the verification goes in the personnel file.

official.notes: No single IDPH document exists. IDPH publishes no policy checklist or provider-manual packet for this license, and the application is submitted on Department-provided forms under § 295.500. The list above is therefore built from the regulation sections that require written policies and plans, and it is incomplete. Retrieved in full: § 295.500(a), § 295.2000 and § 295.3000. Retrieved only as search excerpts: § 295.2030 (items (a)(2), (a)(3) and any items past (b)(5) were not shown), § 295.2040 (a partial list of plan elements; (b)(2) onward and the drill-evaluation contents were not shown), § 295.2050 and § 295.2060 (subsections (c) and (d) of § 295.2060 are evidentiary and violation-citation rules, not policy content, so I left them out). Not retrieved at all: §§ 295.2010, 295.2020, 295.2070 and 295.2080, § 295.3010–3050 (including training), Subpart D (including infection control, § 295.4045, which the excerpt shows requiring written policies for investigating, controlling, preventing and testing for infections), Subpart E (medications), Subpart F (resident rights), Subpart G (records), Subpart H (food service/menus) and § 295.2060's cross-references. Fetch those on ilga.gov or law.cornell.edu before relying on this list. Items are paraphrased in part and may not match the rule text word for word, so verify against the official text. ILGA's EntirePart page was blocked during retrieval, and the Cornell LII mirrors were used for the full texts. The Act was amended by Public Act 104-0589 (effective 7/24/2026), and I did not review it for changes to these items. Expected organization: the rules do not prescribe a manual format. A practical manual follows the Part 295 section order above, with one policy per rule section and the rule citation printed on each policy. At the application stage, the proof of the quality improvement program (§ 295.500(a)(8)), the service and contract documents (§ 295.500(a)(10) and (12)) and the disaster plan are the policy-type items the Department checks. Medicaid payment is a separate track. The HFS Supportive Living Program (89 Ill. Adm. Code 146) has its own application and was not reviewed here.
